extracted.intended_audience: NIH SBIR/STTR applicants and NIH peer reviewers (NIAID study section); grant applicants preparing responses to review
extracted.subtask_description: A summary statement and peer review critique for an NIH SBIR (R43) Phase I application evaluating a diagnostic assay proposal using standard NIH review criteria and administrative/compliance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or critical barrier to progress in the field? (Example text: 'A significant global health concern, critical clinical need, and incredibly innovative approach are strengths of this application.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths (e.g., public health importance, potential to improve diagnosis/treatment, ability to reduce testing algorithm from two tests to one) and weaknesses (here: 'None noted'). Includes discussion of the clinical need (rapid, accurate diagnosis of LASV), public health impact, and limitations of current assays (high genetic diversity prevents pan-lineage detection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD(s)/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? (Example text: summaries of PI and team qualifications: 'Iain MacLeod...co-founder and the CSO of Aldatu Biosciences...'; 'Nicholas Renzette...Lead Scientist...co-developed PANDAA')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note relevant training, prior accomplishments, and team composition. Strengths recorded when investigators have demonstrated expertise in the proposed methods and commercialization experience; weaknesses noted when absent (here: 'None noted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms? (Example text: 'PANDAA enables probe-based qPCR for target detection in highly variable genomic regions by simultaneously adapting and amplifying diverse templates.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers enumerate why the approach is novel (e.g., modifications introduced during PCR, capturing unique SNPs, enhancing sensitivity through reaction optimization) and whether there are any innovation-related weaknesses (here: 'None noted').

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the aims? (Example text: 'Aim 1 will determine the optimal primers and probe sequences. Aim 2 will refine the reagents on divergent genomes. Aim 3 will validate the PANDAA diagnostic prototype, analytically and clinically.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess feasibility, preliminary data, experimental design, and risk mitigation (e.g., use of invariant/degenerate bases, universal base 5-nitroindole, comparison with gold-standard RT-PCR, optimization of MgCl2 and primer concentrations). Weaknesses and gaps are specified (e.g., little mention of reverse transcriptase step source; need to analyze L segment; risk of off-target amplification and sequencing verification as mitigation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? (Example text: 'Aldatu is housed in the Harvard Life Lab...All necessary equipment is available for this study.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers cite institutional resources, core facilities, collaborator support, and whether the environment is adequate. Strengths include access to sequencing cores, BSL-2/3 facilities, and supportive incubator programs; weaknesses noted when specialized facilities (e.g., BSL-4) are lacking for proposed select agent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Impact Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall impact reflects the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved. (Example text: 'Impact Score:10' and 'Overall Impact: PANDAA for universal, pan-lineage molecular detection of Lassa fever infection.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring process explained: 'The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion of an application by averaging the overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers on the committee and multiplying by 10.' Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Reviewers provide narrative justifications that feed into the overall impact evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether human subjects protections are adequate or applicable. (Example text: 'Protections for Human Subjects: Not Applicable')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate risks, consent, and protections; here, Not Applicable is noted when no human subjects are involved. Human Subjects is a required review section and influences funding decisions if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the use of vertebrate animals is justified and humane. (Example text: 'Vertebrate Animals: Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals)')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers evaluate animal care, procedures, and justification; absence of animals is noted as Not Applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biohazard risks and whether proposed protections are acceptable. (Example text: Critique 1: 'Biohazards: Unacceptable' with explanation regarding Lassa virus being a Risk Group 4 agent and unclear whether Aldatu would receive virus or extracted RNA; later critiques note 'Biohazards: Acceptable')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers examine biosafety level access, transfer of isolates vs. extracted materials, and institutional containment. Specific concerns (e.g., lack of BSL-4 at applicant site, unclear material transfer) can render the biohazard review unacceptable; mitigation (clear plans, collaborators with containment) can change assessment to acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of issues related to select agents and whether proposed work involves them. (Example text: 'Select Agents: Unacceptable' in one critique; other sections: 'Not Applicable' or 'Acceptable')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note if select agent policies apply, whether access/handling plans are clear, and whether institutional approvals are in place. Lack of clarity may result in an unacceptable rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for sharing data, model organisms, and other resources. (Example text: 'Resource Sharing Plans: Not Applicable' or 'Acceptable')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether resource sharing plans are acceptable and adequate for community use. When not applicable, reviewers note so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to authenticate biological and chemical resources. (Example text: 'Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources: Acceptable')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers check whether applicants describe authentication procedures for cell lines, reagents, and other key resources; acceptable plans reduce risk of irreproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether the requested budget and period of support are reasonable and justified. (Example text: 'Recommended budget modifications or possible overlap identified: Acceptable' and 'The budget was recommended as requested.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative note: 'The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers. If an award is planned, the costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on the recommendations outlined below in the COMMITTEE BUDGET RECOMMENDATIONS section.' Reviewers may recommend accept, modify, or recommend as requested; grants staff finalize award calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility / Preliminary Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of preliminary results and whether they support feasibility. (Example text: 'Preliminary studies with LASV templates from multiple lineages show that PANDAA could detect at least five lineages with near equal sensitivity and outperform the current gold standard assay by greater than an order of magnitude.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers weigh preliminary data quality and relevance (e.g., detection of multiple lineages without optimization) as evidence supporting the proposed aims; lack of preliminary data or gaps in methods can be cited as weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to Gold Standard / Metrics for Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed assay will be compared to established methods and have rigorous validation metrics. (Example text: 'Comparison of the PANDAA assay with a gold standard, published RT-PCR assay is valid and offers metrics when optimizing.'; Aim 3 involves analytical and clinical validation with panels to assess sensitivity and specificity.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect direct comparisons to established assays, defined analytical/clinical validation panels, and metrics such as sensitivity and specificity. They note whether collaborators can supply adequate strain panels (e.g., 100 LASV strains) for rigorous testing.
